question: What makes r6's gv about 3 us slower at m=32 than at m=1 (judge pooler 16.86 vs 13.91, qkv 14.76 vs 9.71), when pw11 showed x L2 traffic costs at most about 1 us? pw14 is pw12 unchanged (same bake, same PICK logic; every pw12 kernel's SASS is identical) plus a PROBE ladder on r6's own gv kernel. It reports, from the same _time_us, how the time builds up from the bare W stream to the full kernel at m=1/8 and m=32, plus two register-cap probes and the pw12 bulk ring's bare stream at m=32.

probes.format: PROBE gvlad <layer> m=<m> <step> <us> regs=<numRegs from cudaFuncGetAttributes> ctas/sm=<cudaOccupancy co-resident CTAs / SMs>
probes.steps: L0 = r6's ld.global W stream only, consumed by an XOR into one register (no x, decode, mma, reduction or store). L1 = + x loads (XOR-consumed). L2 = + decode (the 12-bit decode and escape walk; A and B XOR-consumed). L3 = + mma (no reduction or store). L4 = r6's real pick for the shape (its geometry name, regs and CTAs/SM printed). The steps are V bits 9-11 of the same template, so everything else is r6's code.
probes.geometries: r6's judge picks (job 23cecdef1bb54c9e). pooler m=1/8: (2,16,8,1,1,0) rolled, 1024 thr. pooler m=32: (1,8,16,1,1,2). qkv m=1/8: (1,8,16,1,1,0). qkv m=32: (1,4,16,2,1,2) ST 1, cluster 2.
probes.coverage: m=1 and m=8 share the MT=1 kernels: L0 and L3, then L4. m=32: L0, L1, L2, L3, L4. m=16: L4 only, because a full m=16 ladder would exceed the 16-kernel cap.
probes.occupancy: m=32 full kernel with the __launch_bounds__ minBlocks override (V bits 12-14). pooler cap64 = 4 CTAs x 256 thr, the register cap of r6's m=1 pooler instance (64): ptxas 64 regs but 1520 B spill, so it also measures what spilling costs. pooler cap255 = 1 CTA/SM, 152 regs, 0 spill. qkv cap255: 142 regs, 0 spill. r6's m=1 qkv instance is already uncapped (106 regs), so qkv gets only the cap255 probe.
probes.bulk: L0-bulk8 = the pw12 bulk-ring load path (8 slots, no proxy fence) at the pooler m=32 geometry, XOR-consumed: 59 regs. Compare with pooler m=32 L0 (register loads).
probes.count: 16 probe kernels. Ladder-only compile 6.7 s locally.

reading_guide: L0(m=32) vs L0(m=1): the W stream itself at the m=32 geometry (256 thr, 2 CTAs/SM) vs the m=1 geometry (1024 thr, 1 CTA/SM).
L1 - L0: x loads (L1/L2 traffic plus LSU wavefronts). pw11 bounds this at about 1 us.
L2 - L1: decode. It should not depend on m, since decode is shared by all token tiles.
L3 - L2: mma issue and latency, about 4x more HMMA at m=32 than at m=8.
L4 - L3: in-CTA reduction plus epilogue (qkv m=32 also includes the cluster-2 DSMEM step).
cap255 / cap64 vs L4: whether registers, through occupancy, limit bytes in flight.
caveats: With no compute in the way, ptxas hoists every W load in L0/L1. The m=32 L0 SASS issues all 48 LDG.E.NA.128 of the warp's 16 chunks up front (126 regs), where r6's real kernel keeps ST=2. L0 at m=32 is therefore the stream of that grid at maximum per-warp depth, an upper bound on what the load path delivers, not r6's depth. pooler m=1 L0 keeps r6's ST=1 rolled loop (SASS: 3 LDG + 6 LOP3 per iteration). The bulk-ring L0 has the same caveat in its favour (ring-limited depth).
L1 and L3 at m=32 hit the 128-register cap and spill 16-72 B (the XOR consumers lengthen live ranges). That is small next to the effects being looked for, but noted.
The probes are compiled for the r6 geometries of job 23cecdef1bb54c9e. If r6's bake picks a different geometry on the day, L4 prints the picked name and the ladder still describes the job's geometry.
kill_if: Not a speed candidate. The bake and PICK are pw12's, so pw14's own score only re-measures pw12. Success = every PROBE gvlad line present and the m=32 gap attributed (the L0..L4 steps summing to L4 within noise).
local_checks: nvcc 12.8 -Xptxas -v: 153 kernels (137 pw12 + 16 probes). pw12's 137 kernels are SASS-identical; the one diff is the ptxasOptions metadata string. lint ok; cpu-check --official 9/9.
